A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FasterCache with the same authors, core method, and principal experiments. All 19 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original acceleration benchmarks, component ablations, scalability experiments, generated examples, and a human preference study in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds feature-approximation analyses, sensitivity tests, additional comparator results, and larger-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The dynamic feature reuse and frequency-dependent CFG-Cache procedures in Equations (5)–(11) remain unchanged, including their default schedules. Learned weights and second-order corrections appear as experimental alternatives; they do not replace the proposed training-free method.

E1.justification: The VBench prompt benchmark and text-to-video, image-to-video, and image-generation tasks are retained. Appendix A.3.3 adds an explicit empty-versus-nonempty negative-prompt comparison, extending the tested conditioning scenarios. The additional base models do not themselves establish new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PAB to the CogVideoX and Vchitect-2.0 comparisons, where v1 evaluated only the original model, Delta-DiT variants, and FasterCache. PAB already appeared in the other model comparisons; those comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce CogVideoX-5B at 48 frames/480P and Mochi-10B at 163 frames/480P, controlled weight and caching-interval settings, and feature-approximation evaluation using approximately 200 videos and L1 distance. These extend the evaluation protocol without revising the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, Appendices A.3 and A.5.2 add first- versus second-order approximation analysis, constant/learned/linear weight comparisons, CFG-bias visualizations, negative-prompt and guidance-scale robustness tests, and caching-interval and enhancement-weight sensitivity studies. These substantially expand evidence about why the design works and when fidelity declines.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The human study retains 30 videos per model and five raters per sample. The approximately 200 videos in the new feature analysis specify its sample size, not repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark and human-preference results are retained. New results include PAB latencies of 57.98 seconds on CogVideoX and 206.23 seconds on Vchitect-2.0, extensive approximation and sensitivity results, and reported speedups of 1.63× on CogVideoX-5B and 1.74× on Mochi-10B. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces a smoothness assumption and Taylor/finite-difference derivation for feature reuse in Equations (12)–(15), plus mathematical conditions and approximations for CFG-bias reuse in Equations (16)–(18). This analytical treatment was absent from v1 and goes beyond restating the unchanged method equations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free acceleration through dynamic feature reuse and CFG-Cache while preserving video quality. The headline Vchitect-2.0 claim remains 1.67× speedup with VBench scores of 80.80% for the original model and 80.84% for FasterCache.

C2.justification: v2 adds focused explanations for choosing first-order corrections and linear weights, connects CFG frequency changes to layout versus detail synthesis, and interprets the new robustness tests. It also argues that stronger base models improve handling of complex motion. The existing limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the exact nonempty negative prompt and explains the MSE objective used to fit the learned-weight experimental alternative. It also identifies the retained CogVideoX qualitative examples as the 2B model. The code link, A100 hardware, PyTorch/FlashAttention setup, and original default hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Hsiao et al.'s diffusion distillation work, Meng et al.'s guided diffusion distillation, VideoElevator, and Mochi. Hsiao et al. is explicitly connected to the CFG interpretation. The Vchitect-2.0 reference is updated to its paper rather than representing a new research direction.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact, with localized wording edits and appendix cross-references. The appendix gains a discussion section and additional subheadings, while existing qualitative results and the user study are retained under new numbering. Acknowledgements and the ICLR publication header are also added.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial analytical displays in Figures 13–16, larger-model examples in Figure 21, and Tables 5, 7, and 8. Existing appendix galleries and the human-study table are retained and renumbered. Main-text refinements include expanded captions, a CFG-Cache onset marker, and correction of Table 3's swapped PSNR/SSIM headers.

improvement.justification: The added design-choice and sensitivity studies better support previously heuristic choices, and the new PAB rows close gaps in the comparisons. However, the new analytical support has a coefficient error: Equation (13) uses 3 instead of 9 for the second-order Taylor term. Table 8 also reports interval-9 LPIPS of 0.0104, conflicting with the stated fidelity-degradation trend. The empirical additions and clearer documentation provide a net improvement, but these inconsistencies limit its strength.
